chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukayr,
regarding the child of the free man and the slave woman, he said: 'He goes to the free one from them'.

key_terms.يَذْهَبُ إِلَى: he goes to / is attributed to

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a child born to a free man and a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, articulates the principle of 'dhahab ila al-hurr' (going to the free), which dictates that a child born to a free father and a slave mother inherits the father's free status. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining lineage and manumission, ensuring the child is not bound by the mother's servitude. It reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on freeing slaves and clarifying social status through paternal lineage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, and Al Hakam Bin Miskeen, from Jameel, and Ibn Bukeyr,
‘With regards to the child from the free man and the slave woman, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would go to the free one from them’.
